technical: Crawlability scores 100 of 100: robots.txt readable, one sitemap, HTTPS, canonical tags correct on 171 of 171 pages, no accidental noindex, every URL answering.

All eight crawlers checked are allowed, including GPTBot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot, CCBot and Google-Extended. AI access scores 94 of 100 against visualedgeit.com at 100; the gap is llms.txt, which is not published.
Answer-shaped content scores 21 of 100, the lowest component on the scorecard.
FAQPage markup on 4 of 110 service, industry and location pages; question headings on 23 of 110; Service or Article schema on 3 of 113 buyer and blog pages.
Review or AggregateRating schema is absent from all 171 pages, and BreadcrumbList from all 171.
Average page length is 463 words; 65 pages sit under 300 words; 59 pages grade D or F and three grade A.
Internal linking is strong: all 141 service, industry, location and company pages carry ten or more internal links, money pages 88 to 114.
Every money page carries a branded Open Graph image; none of the nine uses a stock image.

Authority Score 21 from 510 referring domains and 2,687 backlinks. One domain, indianaruralhealth.org, is the source of 45.6 percent of all links, and 46.5 percent of links carry no anchor text because they are logos.
The sitemap lists 325 blog URLs of the form /blog?p=. A crawler following links from the site reaches three posts.
implications: The build applies the /copiers/ template, the only page type on the site scoring above 85, to every money page: question headings, FAQPage and Service schema together.
Indianapolis gets a hub page that links to all nine money pages, which is the single change with the most measured demand behind it.
The ten thin location pages are rebuilt, starting with Columbus and South Bend, the two with measured demand.
llms.txt and BreadcrumbList are published, closing the two free access signals the analysis flags.
Review markup waits for real Google reviews; no competitor in this market has it either, so it stays the differentiating signal rather than a shortcut.
